buyer_question: An internal CLI tool we are inheriting depends on PyInquirer for its interactive prompts — does the README's pip install path and quickstart import still work on a current Python, is the documented prompt_toolkit workaround valid, is the CI badge real, and is the project maintained?

claims.text: The command `pip install PyInquirer` completes successfully on a current Python (resolving and installing the package and its declared dependencies).
claims.source_quote:
Simply use pip to install the PyInquirer package

.. code:: shell

    pip install PyInquirer
claims.probe_hint: python3 -m venv /tmp/v && /tmp/v/bin/pip install PyInquirer && /tmp/v/bin/pip list | grep -i -E 'pyinquirer|prompt'

claims.text: After `pip install PyInquirer`, the README quickstart import `from PyInquirer import prompt, print_json` succeeds on a current Python interpreter.
claims.source_quote:
from __future__ import print_function, unicode_literals
    from PyInquirer import prompt, print_json
claims.probe_hint: /tmp/v/bin/python -c 'from PyInquirer import prompt, print_json; print("ok")'  # expect ImportError: cannot import name Mapping from collections (prompt_toolkit 1.0.14) on Python >= 3.10

claims.text: If a prompt_toolkit error is encountered, installing the version the README prescribes with `pip install prompt_toolkit==1.0.14` resolves it and makes PyInquirer importable.
claims.source_quote:
In case you encounter any prompt\_toolkit error, that means you've the
wrong prompt\_toolkit version.

You can correct that by doing

.. code:: shell

    pip install prompt_toolkit==1.0.14
claims.probe_hint: /tmp/v/bin/pip install prompt_toolkit==1.0.14 && /tmp/v/bin/python -c 'import prompt_toolkit.styles.from_dict'  # inspect prompt_toolkit/styles/from_dict.py line 9

claims.text: With PyInquirer importable, `prompt(questions)` for a list containing one `{'type': 'input', 'name': 'first_name', 'message': ...}` question returns a dict keyed by 'first_name', which `print_json(answers)` prints as JSON.
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "import pexpect; c=pexpect.spawn('/tmp/v/bin/python examples/input.py'); c.expect('first name'); c.sendline('Bob'); c.expect(pexpect.EOF, timeout=20); print(c.before.decode())"  # needs a pty and an interpreter where c2 imports

claims.text: The repository ships example scripts editor.py, expand.py, list.py, password.py, when.py, checkbox.py, confirm.py, hierarchical.py, pizza.py, input.py and rawlist.py under ./examples/.

Running `pip install -e .` inside a clone of the repository yields a working from-source install in which the quickstart import `from PyInquirer import prompt, print_json` succeeds, so the examples can be launched with repository code.
claims.source_quote:
If you want to launch examples with the code from repository instead of
installing a package you need to execute ``pip install -e .`` within project
directory.
claims.probe_hint: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CITGuru/PyInquirer /tmp/pyinq && cd /tmp/pyinq && python3 -m venv .v && .v/bin/pip install -e . && .v/bin/python -c 'from PyInquirer import prompt, print_json'  # check PyInquirer/__init__.py: the prompt import is commented out at HEAD

claims.text: PyInquirer supports the question types input, confirm, list, rawlist, expand, checkbox, password and editor (one prompt implementation per type).
claims.source_quote:
-  ``type``: (String) Type of the prompt. Defaults: input - Possible values:
   input, confirm, list, rawlist, expand, checkbox, password, editor
claims.probe_hint: gh api repos/CITGuru/PyInquirer/contents/PyInquirer/prompts?ref=7637373429bec66788650cda8091b7a6f12929ee --jq '.[].name'  # expect a module per type

claims.text: The Travis CI badge in the README (travis-ci.org/expobrain/PyInquirer, branch master) asserts a live, passing CI build for the project.
claims.probe_hint: curl -sL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n' 'https://travis-ci.org/expobrain/PyInquirer.svg?branch=master'  # travis-ci.org shut down 2021; note the badge points at a fork owner, not CITGuru

claims.text: The documented contributor flow — `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `pip install -r requirements_dev.txt`, then `pytest -sv tests/` in a clone — installs cleanly and the test suite passes on a current Python.
claims.source_quote:
$ pip install -r requirements.txt
    $ pip install -r requirements_dev.txt

With an environment ready you can add new feature and check everything works
just fine

.. code:: shell

    $ pytest -sv tests/
claims.probe_hint: cd /tmp/pyinq && .v/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements_dev.txt && .v/bin/pytest -sv tests/ -x -q 2>&1 | tail -20

claims.text: The project is looking for a successor/maintainer, as announced in GitHub issue #159 on CITGuru/PyInquirer (i.e. the issue exists and is still open).
claims.source_quote: **Update: We are looking for a successor/maintainance. Here: <https://github.com/CITGuru/PyInquirer/issues/159>**
claims.probe_hint: gh api repos/CITGuru/PyInquirer/issues/159 --jq '"\(.title) \(.state) \(.created_at)"'; gh api repos/CITGuru/PyInquirer --jq '.pushed_at'

claims.text: PyInquirer 1.0.3 is the current bugfix release, published at github.com/CITGuru/PyInquirer/releases/tag/1.0.3 and matching the latest version on PyPI.
claims.probe_hint: gh api repos/CITGuru/PyInquirer/releases/tags/1.0.3 --jq '.published_at'; curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/PyInquirer/json | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['info']['version'], d['releases'][d['info']['version']][0]['upload_time'])"
